## 1. Libraries and input checks

```{r wc_dat, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
WC_dat <- read.csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "DF_water_quality_data_2026.csv")
) %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = ymd_hms(datetime, tz = "UTC"),
    datetime = with_tz(datetime, tzone = local_tz),
    date = as.Date(datetime, tz = local_tz),
    year = year(datetime),
    mon = month(datetime),
    jday = yday(datetime),
    burn_lab = case_when(
      site_lab == "ophir" ~ "unburned",
      site_lab %in% c(
        "davis",
        "winters_usgs",
        "winters_up",
        "browns",
        "browns_sub"
      ) ~ "burn",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Sites used throughout the DMC workflow
sites_keep <- c("winters_usgs", "ophir")
site_labels <- c(winters_usgs = "Winters USGS", ophir = "Ophir")

# Set start and end deliberately: these dates define the cumulative-volume baseline.
analysis_start <- as.Date("2024-10-15")
analysis_end   <- as.Date("2026-05-14")
fire_date      <- as.Date("2024-09-25")  # containment date; used for plot color

# Set FALSE to exclude below-detection-limit substituted concentrations.
include_bdl <- TRUE
```


For each chemistry sample, the measured concentration is assumed representative of the water volume **since the preceding chemistry sample** (the first sample represents the period since the analysis start date). Interval loads are estimates, not measured continuous loads. A chemistry value with a missing discharge day in its interval is **not** assigned a load; the default analysis starts a new complete series after such a gap and does not silently sum across missing intervals. The analysis uses one common observation window for both sites and each analyte's available chemistry observations.

Normalized cumulative load versus normalized cumulative water volume is fitted with a regression through the origin. The fitted slope is a descriptive summary of DMC curvature, **not** a direct concentration–discharge exponent or an independent-observation significance test. Because cumulative observations are serially dependent and both normalized series end near (1,1), inferential p-values and CIs from ordinary `lm` are exploratory only.


## 2. Chemistry analytes and units

The original script used `TSS`, but the updated object has `TSS_QC`. The source's `togL` values were mislabeled as g/L conversions; here everything is converted explicitly to **mg/L**, then mg/L × liters / 1000 gives grams.

```{r analytes}
## Analyte definitions and unit conversions
analytes <- tribble(
  ~analyte, ~col,       ~unit,  ~to_mg_L,
  "DOC",    "DOC_QC",    "mg/L", 1,
  "TOC",    "TOC_QC",    "mg/L", 1,
  "TDN",    "TDN_QC",    "mg/L", 1,
  "PO4_P",  "PO4.P_QC",  "mg/L", 1,
  "NO3_N",  "NO3.N_QC",  "mg/L", 1,
  "NH4_N",  "NH4.N_QC",  "mg/L", 1,
  "TSS",    "TSS_QC",    "mg/L", 1,
  "Al",     "Al_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "As",     "As_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "B",      "B_QC",      "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Ba",     "Ba_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Ca",     "Ca_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Cr",     "Cr_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Fe",     "Fe_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Mn",     "Mn_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Pb",     "Pb_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Sr",     "Sr_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001,
  "Zn",     "Zn_QC",     "µg/L", 0.001
)

# Check that all required analytes are present
missing_cols <- setdiff(analytes$col, names(WC_dat))

if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing analyte columns: ",
    paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


stopifnot(nrow(analytes) > 0)

# Match lab detection flags, when available; a blank flag is not a BDL flag.
analytes <- analytes %>%
  mutate(dl_col = sub("_QC$", "_DL_lab", col),
         dl_col = if_else(dl_col %in% names(WC_dat), dl_col, NA_character_))
```

```{r flow_dat, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE }

# Daily discharge and precipitation observations
df_hydro <- read.csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "hydro_clim_WY2024_2026.csv")
) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
```

## 3. Prepare continuous daily hydrology

Daily `Q` must be m3/s. `NA` is preserved; only a measured zero is treated as zero

```{r flow}
flow_daily <- df_hydro %>%
  transmute(site = tolower(trimws(as.character(site))),
            date = as.Date(date), Q = as.numeric(Q),
            water_year, precip_mm) %>%
  filter(site %in% sites_keep, between(date, analysis_start, analysis_end))

if (anyDuplicated(flow_daily[c("site", "date")])) {
  stop("Duplicate site/date combinations in df_hydro: resolve before estimating loads.")
}

flow_daily <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  site = sites_keep,
  date = seq(analysis_start, analysis_end, by = "day")
) %>%
  left_join(flow_daily, by = c("site", "date")) %>%
  arrange(site, date) %>%
  mutate(Q_daily_liters = if_else(!is.na(Q) & Q >= 0, Q * 86400 * 1000, NA_real_),
         missing_or_invalid_Q = is.na(Q_daily_liters))

flow_coverage <- flow_daily %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(n_days = n(), n_valid_Q = sum(!missing_or_invalid_Q),
            pct_valid_Q = 100 * mean(!missing_or_invalid_Q),
            n_zero_Q = sum(Q == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(flow_coverage, digits = 1)
```

## 4. Prepare water-chemistry observations


```{r chemistry}

# 4. Prepare chemistry observations
chem_wide <- WC_dat %>%
  mutate(
    site = site_lab,
    sample_id = row_number()
  ) %>%
  filter(
    site %in% sites_keep,
    between(date, analysis_start, analysis_end)
  ) %>%
  arrange(site, datetime)


# Detection limit flags
dl_lookup <- analytes %>%
  filter(!is.na(dl_col)) %>%
  select(analyte, dl_col)

flag_long <- chem_wide %>%
  select(
    sample_id,
    any_of(dl_lookup$dl_col)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(dl_lookup$dl_col),
    names_to = "dl_col",
    values_to = "bdl_flag"
  ) %>%
  left_join(dl_lookup, by = "dl_col") %>%
  select(sample_id, analyte, bdl_flag)


# Individual chemistry observations
chem_long <- chem_wide %>%
  select(
    sample_id,
    site,
    date,
    datetime,
    storm,
    all_of(analytes$col)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(analytes$col),
    names_to = "col",
    values_to = "concentration_raw"
  ) %>%
  left_join(analytes, by = "col") %>%
  left_join(
    flag_long,
    by = c("sample_id", "analyte")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    concentration_raw = as.numeric(concentration_raw),
    concentration_mg_L = concentration_raw * to_mg_L,
    tsf = as.integer(date - fire_date)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(concentration_mg_L),
    concentration_mg_L >= 0
  ) %>%
  {
    if (include_bdl) {
      .
    } else {
      filter(., bdl_flag != "yes" | is.na(bdl_flag))
    }
  } %>%
  arrange(site, analyte, datetime, sample_id)


# Daily representative concentrations
chem_daily <- chem_long %>%
  group_by(site, analyte, date) %>%
  summarise(
    concentration_mg_L = median(
      concentration_mg_L,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    n_samples = n(),
    concentration_min = min(concentration_mg_L),
    concentration_max = max(concentration_mg_L),
    first_sample = min(datetime),
    last_sample = max(datetime),
    tsf = first(tsf),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    multiple_samples = n_samples > 1
  ) %>%
  arrange(site, analyte, date)


# Review storm sampling
storm_daily_summary <- chem_daily %>%
  filter(multiple_samples) %>%
  arrange(site, analyte, date)

knitr::kable(
  storm_daily_summary,
  digits = 3
)

```

## 5. Estimate interval water volumes and solute loads

For a sample on date `t_k`, interval volume includes days **after the previous sample date through `t_k`**, inclusive. For the first sample it begins on `analysis_start`. The number of observed daily Q values must equal the number of calendar days in the interval. Missing intervals are flagged and excluded from the contiguous DMC run; subsequent intervals can start a new run. The first interval is only meaningful if the assumed initial chemistry concentration represents the preceding interval.

```{r interval-loads}
# One row per chemistry sample interval, using daily flow observations.

# 5. Estimate interval water volumes and solute loads
chem_intervals <- chem_daily %>%
  group_by(site, analyte) %>%
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    interval_start = lag(
      date,
      default = analysis_start - 1L
    ) + 1L,

    interval_end = date,

    expected_days = as.integer(
      interval_end - interval_start
    ) + 1L
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# Calculate water volume for each interval
interval_flow <- chem_intervals %>%
  select(
    site,
    analyte,
    date,
    interval_start,
    interval_end,
    expected_days
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    flow_daily %>%
      select(
        site,
        flow_date = date,
        Q_daily_liters
      ),
    by = "site",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    flow_date >= interval_start,
    flow_date <= interval_end
  ) %>%
  group_by(site, analyte, date) %>%
  summarise(
    n_valid_Q = sum(!is.na(Q_daily_liters)),

    Q_interval_liters = sum(
      Q_daily_liters,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Calculate solute loads
loads_all <- chem_intervals %>%
  left_join(
    interval_flow,
    by = c("site", "analyte", "date")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_valid_Q = coalesce(n_valid_Q, 0L),

    complete_interval =
      n_valid_Q == expected_days &
      expected_days > 0,

    Q_interval_liters = if_else(
      complete_interval,
      Q_interval_liters,
      NA_real_
    ),

    load_interval_g =
      concentration_mg_L *
      Q_interval_liters / 1000
  ) %>%
  arrange(site, analyte, date) %>%
  group_by(site, analyte) %>%
  mutate(
    run_id = cumsum(!complete_interval),

    in_dmc =
      run_id == 0L &
      complete_interval
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# QC summary
interval_qc <- loads_all %>%
  group_by(site, analyte) %>%
  summarise(
    n_intervals = n(),

    n_complete_intervals = sum(
      complete_interval
    ),

    n_in_dmc = sum(in_dmc),

    n_multiple_sample_days = sum(
      multiple_samples
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(interval_qc)



# The first incomplete interval stops the primary series. If it occurs early,
# change analysis_start to a date with complete Q coverage, then rerun.
dmc_long <- loads_all %>%
  filter(in_dmc) %>%
  group_by(site, analyte) %>%
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    Q_c_liters = cumsum(Q_interval_liters),

    load_cum_g = cumsum(load_interval_g),

    Q_c_norm = if (
      max(Q_c_liters) > 0
    ) {
      Q_c_liters / max(Q_c_liters)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    load_c_norm = if (
      max(load_cum_g) > 0
    ) {
      load_cum_g / max(load_cum_g)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    site = factor(
      site,
      levels = sites_keep,
      labels = unname(site_labels[sites_keep])
    )
  )
```

## 6. DMC slope models and descriptive interpretation

The original script fits `load_c_norm ~ 0 + Q_c_norm`. Retained here for comparability, with the important caveat that normalized cumulative data are not independent. Interpret slopes above/below one as **relative curvature summaries** (enrichment/dilution), not proof of a process. The 1:1 reference is also plotted.

```{r models}
fit_one_dmc <- function(dat) {
  dat <- filter(dat, is.finite(Q_c_norm), is.finite(load_c_norm))
  if (nrow(dat) < 3 || n_distinct(dat$Q_c_norm) < 2) {
    return(tibble(n_samples = nrow(dat), slope = NA_real_, std_error = NA_real_,
                  lwr = NA_real_, upr = NA_real_, p_vs_1 = NA_real_, r_squared = NA_real_))
  }
  fit <- lm(load_c_norm ~ 0 + Q_c_norm, data = dat)
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  slope <- unname(co[1, "Estimate"])
  se <- unname(co[1, "Std. Error"])
  df <- df.residual(fit)
  tcrit <- qt(0.975, df)
  tibble(n_samples = nrow(dat), slope = slope, std_error = se,
         lwr = slope - tcrit * se, upr = slope + tcrit * se,
         p_vs_1 = 2 * pt(abs((slope - 1) / se), df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         r_squared = summary(fit)$r.squared)
}

models_tbl <- dmc_long %>%
  group_by(site, analyte) %>%
  group_modify(~fit_one_dmc(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(interpretation = case_when(
    is.na(slope) ~ "Insufficient data",
    slope > 1 ~ "Relative enrichment (descriptive)",
    slope < 1 ~ "Relative dilution (descriptive)",
    TRUE ~ "Proportional"
  ))

knitr::kable(models_tbl %>% select(site, analyte, n_samples, slope, lwr, upr, p_vs_1, interpretation), digits = 3)
```

## 7. Plot DMCs

```{r plotting-functions}
plot_dmc <- function(analyte_name) {
  dat <- dmc_long %>% filter(analyte == analyte_name)
  mod <- models_tbl %>% filter(analyte == analyte_name, is.finite(slope)) %>%
    mutate(label = sprintf("β = %.2f", slope))
  ggplot(dat, aes(Q_c_norm, load_c_norm)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey65") +
    geom_abline(data = mod, aes(slope = slope, intercept = 0),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_path(color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(aes(color = tsf), size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_text(data = mod, aes(x = 0.05, y = 0.94, label = label),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 4) +
    facet_wrap(~site, nrow = 1, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1, name = "Days since fire") +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Norm. cumulative streamflow",
         y = paste("Norm. cumulative", analyte_name)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

### better visual
# Updated DMC plotting function

plot_dmc <- function(analyte_name) {

  dat <- dmc_long %>%
    filter(analyte == analyte_name)

  mod <- models_tbl %>%
    filter(
      analyte == analyte_name,
      is.finite(slope)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      label = sprintf("β = %.2f", slope)
    )

  ggplot(dat, aes(Q_c_norm, load_c_norm)) +

    # 1:1 reference line
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "grey65",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +

    # Estimated slope
    geom_abline(
      data = mod,
      aes(slope = slope, intercept = 0),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +

    # Cumulative trajectory
    geom_path(
      color = "grey55",
      linewidth = 0.6,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +

    # Observations
    geom_point(
      aes(color = tsf),
      size = 2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +

    # Slope annotations
    geom_text(
      data = mod,
      aes(
        x = 0.05,
        y = 0.88,
        label = label
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 2.7
    ) +

    # Site panels
    facet_wrap(
      ~site,
      nrow = 1,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +

    # Color scale
    scale_color_viridis_c(
      option = "plasma",
      direction = -1,
      name = "Days since fire"
    ) +

    # Consistent axes
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 1),
      breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 1),
      breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)
    ) +

    coord_equal() +

    # Individual panel title only
    labs(
      title = analyte_name,
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +

    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +

    theme(
      # Title
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 13,
        face = "bold",
        hjust = 0.5,
        margin = margin(b = 6)
      ),

      # Facet labels
      strip.text = element_text(
        size = 9,
        face = "bold"
      ),

      # Axis tick labels
      axis.text = element_text(
        size = 8,
        color = "black"
      ),

      # Remove individual axis titles
      axis.title = element_blank(),

      # Grid
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(
        color = "grey90",
        linewidth = 0.3
      ),

      # Spacing between site facets
      panel.spacing.x = unit(0.25, "cm"),

      # Legend
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),

      # Margins
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
}
```

## 8. Residual diagnostics

These are residuals from the descriptive normalized DMC regression. Their cumulative sum is a visual diagnostic only, not a formal independent-error change-point test.

```{r residuals}
residuals_long <- dmc_long %>%
  left_join(models_tbl %>% select(site, analyte, slope), by = c("site", "analyte")) %>%
  mutate(fitted_norm = slope * Q_c_norm,
         resid_norm = load_c_norm - fitted_norm) %>%
  group_by(site, analyte) %>%
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(cumul_resid = cumsum(resid_norm)) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_dmc_residuals <- function(analyte_name) {
  residuals_long %>%
    filter(analyte == analyte_name) %>%
    ggplot(aes(date, cumul_resid)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey65") +
    geom_line(color = "grey45") +
    geom_point(aes(color = tsf), size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~site, nrow = 1) + #scales = "free_y")
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1,
                          name = "Days since fire") +
    labs(title = paste("DMC residuals:", analyte_name),
         x = NULL, y = "Residual") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

### Flow time series

```{r,  fig.width=15, fig.height=4, out.width="99%", echo=F, include=TRUE}
ref_date <- as.Date("2024-09-25")


# Site order and labels
site_order <- c(
    "winters_usgs",
    "ophir"
)

site_strip_labs_v2 <- c(
  winters_usgs = "Winters USGS",
  ophir        = "Ophir"
)


plot_start <- as.Date("2024-10-14")
plot_end   <- as.Date("2026-05-14")


# Prepare hydrograph data for plotting

flow_plot_dat <- df_hydro %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    tsf  = as.integer(difftime(date, ref_date, units = "days")),
    site = factor(as.character(site), levels = site_order),
    flow_plot = dplyr::coalesce(Q, Q)
  ) %>%
  filter(site == "winters_usgs" | site == "ophir", date > plot_start, date < plot_end) %>%
  arrange(site, tsf)



# Plot

flow_density_plt <- ggplot(
  flow_plot_dat,
  aes(x = tsf, y = flow_plot)
) +
  # new color scale for tsf-colored flow
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
  geom_segment(
    aes(xend = tsf, y = 0, yend = flow_plot, color = tsf),
    linewidth = 1.1,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(color = tsf),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~site,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y",
    labeller = labeller(site = as_labeller(site_strip_labs_v2))
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma",
    direction = -1,
    name = "Days since fire"
  ) +
  # scale_y_continuous(
  #   limits = c(min(flow_segments_plot_tsf$seg_y, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.2, NA)
  # ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(Streamflow~(m^3~s^-1))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.9, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 10.5, 0, 10.5),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, angle = 90, vjust = 0.5)
  )

flow_density_plt
```
